notes.title: New Level: Ground Meat -- Final Update!
notes.content:
It was a grueling process, but PsiloSybil development is finally over: update 1.0.1, with the final level [b]Ground Meat[/b], bringing the total to 25 fully playable and unique levels, is here.

Ground Meat is a rather macabre level set in decomposing carcasses under the forest floor. It has a sidescrolling section and, a PsiloSybil first, a [b]mascot riding section[/b]! Yes, believe your eyes ball, we have the riding section. The level is long, but on the easier side. The NPC mushroom is... well, you should see for yourselves.

I have cancer. This is obviously a pressing matter and I really want that when it comes for me to address it, I know that PS is something I can proudly claim to have completed, and can deliver in a respectable state which reflects the spirit of the original project I started way too many years ago. A core of simple, straightforward atoms (you can jump, you can run, spikes will kill you, get that collectible...) assembled into intricate sequences that can offer a challenge far greater than the sum of its parts. PsiloSybil is an experiment in game design, in how small can we make a grammar in which truly devilish sentences can still be formed. I've learned a lot from it, and I'm very glad I got to make it. Now it's your time, to play it, to break it, to take it apart and alphabetize the pieces, or let it ruin you, or drive the controller into the f***ing monitor. Whatever you want to do with it, it's yours to use as you please.

This is the last content update. I will continue providing support and bugfixes in the coming days. Soon I will announce the official release of the game and finally pass this strange creature to you, the players. It's about time we stopped developing and started playing!

If you notice any bugs, please report them in the discussion forum here or in the discord server, so that I can quickly address them!

[b]Version 1.0.1 -- The Last Update[/b]

[b]New level Ground Meat released[/b]
- In a late-beta to final stage. Located between Citrus Falls and Chef Porcini. NPC mushroom is Chaim. Skull times are set. Life tokens are set.
- Chaim is now required to get Peter in the Tower.

[b]Arcade Mode[/b]
- NPC mushrooms now appear in arcade mode, and can be talked to. They have new custom dialogue lines for arcade. Tokens and shroom platforms still don't exist in arcade mode.
- In Dark Chocolate, an unreachable life token was removed.
- The shroom platform hint inscription in Crystal Hollow doesn't appear in arcade mode.

- Death counter text after level end has more variants
- In the Tower, requirements are displayed in a more readable fashion
[b]
Generic[/b]

notes.title: Patch Notes 1.0.0-d
notes.content:
[b]Gameplay[/b]
- [b]Killed enemies now play an animation[/b] (slapped away or bounced on). The trajectory makes a rough attempt to avoid obstacles. This is not yet implemented for a few enemies in the game for which there are some technical complications. The yellow boarcerers in Wizard Giza now become fully visible when killed.

- Active cycle timers will now instantly halt when Sybil dies, avoiding situations in which enemies or platforms pass right through Sybil while she's playing a death animation. This does not yet affect processes that are not timed to a cycle and do their own timing, such as the boars with the fork in Close Encounters.

[b]Settings[/b]

notes.title: Beta 0.7.4 - Last Stretch
notes.content:
Hello people,

I apologize yet again for a prolonged period with no updates. Sadly I have had some health issues to take care of. Now I'm back to Psilosybil development and I'd like to finish cleaning up the very last things before we can officially call it done!

Now it's possible you may have missed it, but there are many new levels! The latest levels added are

[list]
[*] [b]Platformer Level[/b] - an extremely challenging bonus!
[*] [b]Truffle Traffic[/b] - a fun, mid-game session of highway hopping
[*] [b]Dark Chocolate[/b] - the higher road.
[/list]

Make sure to check them out if these don't sound familiar!

Here's patch notes for this specific small update:

[b]Beta 0.7.4[/b]

[b]Citrus Falls, Cliffhanger, The Tower[/b]
- Fixed a long-standing bug that would make thrown lemons be much slower on certain systems.
[b]Dessert Outpost[/b]
- It's now much easier and more consistent to kill the chocolate bunnies by bouncing on them. This does not invalidate previous runs.
[b]Arcade Mode[/b]
- Fixed a bug whereas entering a level normally after a game over would re-trigger the game over screen.
- The game over screen is now correctly coloured black in HD mode.
[b]Platformer Level[/b]
- Fixed a bug where platforms could not despawn correctly if the player could execute a segment without dying.
[b]Generic[/b]
- Standardized mushroom species names.

notes.title: New Level: Dark Chocolate
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40950640/ba0f5aaa50aa43b3273eaa6459f3a6150e69b525.png[/img]

Short and sweet but ruthless and tricky, newest level Dark Chocolate is sure to humble the overconfident PsiloSybil [strike]vict[/strike] player. This level is located between Haunted Lodge and Hell's Bells. If you have freed Markab from Close Encounters, you will have access to an early exit that will let you skip the tough ending section. You also need Markab to collect all the tokens and free this level's mushroom friend Letitia. Letitia is [b]tough[/b]! And so are the time trials. No mercy to be found in this slippery realm, but it is fairly short so it shouldn't be [i]too[/i] frustrating.

Also recently introduced you will find a renewed Sybil model with all animations redone and new ones added, in addition to two additional Steam Achievements.

Letitia is a true puzzle, see if you can figure this one out. Markab is a requirement for the tokens and also he allows you to access an early exit for this very slippery level.

notes.title: New Boss Fight: Chef Porcini
notes.content:
A bit of unplanned radio silence due to the data loss catastrophe and having to set up shop on a completely different dev machine altogether. One step at a time I recover.

One such step is newest boss fight [b]Chef Porcini[/b], which is the first true new gameplay content since then. It's the fourth and probably-ish last boss to be added to the game, but it's the first you will meet in the game and it's honestly really, really easy. Still fun though. I think at least one thing in this game ought to be easy. That's ok. I accept it.

Level count is now up to 20. Probably will pump out a few more and then wrap this strange-looking game thing up for a final release.

See ya psilo heads

notes.title: Like a phoenix from the ashes. 0.6
notes.content:
Maybe you know, maybe you don't, last month my hard drive died. It was an absolute disaster. We almost lost all of Psilosybil's source code. So if you're wondering why there haven't been much news for a bit, that was why.

Thankfully I had an almost complete and very recent backup, but it took a lot of patient work to reconstruct the missing parts, mostly in the audio. The [b]newest reborn build[/b] is made on a new machine, and is essentially an almost perfect replica of the original in the parts that were missing, and it also has some new goodies, which I really hope you enjoy. Because of this traumatic journey and also because some cool new features got smuggled in with the restoration, I'm marking this as a major version, 0.6. Here's what's new:

- [b]New and improved time trial ghost system[/b]. Ghosts are now saved independently from the main save file, and you can have as many as you like on each level. After a successful time trial, you will now be prompted to set a three-letter name to sign your ghost with. And before starting a time trial, if you have any ghosts saved you can choose to race any one of them, or disable the ghost. Ghosts display an icon specific to the skin you used. Ghost files can be easily copied and passed to other people.
- All previous ghosts are incompatible and will be unreadable starting from this version. Your skulls and best times will be preserved and work correctly, just the actual ghost will not be accessible and might even get deleted from your file. If you care about preserving old ghosts, please back up your savefile and get in touch with me about converting them to the new format.
- Pause menu during a time trial now displays the target times for the bronze and gold skulls.
- Changes to the skin selection screen.
- Due to loss of several audio sources in certain uncompressed formats, there might be differences in audio in some parts of the game, especially in relative volume. In some cases I've changed things for the better, like in P.E.A.R.L., but there might be spots where it is unintentionally different or buggy. Please pay attention and report any anomaly.

notes.title: Two New Levels: "Crystal Hollow" and "Gruesome Grotto", + new "Feline" Skin
notes.content:
Hi!

We march on with PsiloSybil development. This update comes with two sibling levels with two sibling NPCs.

The first one is [b]Crystal Hollow[/b], an early-game spelunk session through a dark, mysterious cave. It's pretty easy but it's fun. You can have fun freeing the resident mushroom friend Rory. You can find the level right after Roach Motel.

The second new cave level is [b]Gruesome Grotto[/b], which is much harder and introduces even more mind-bending mechanics. See if you can free Rory's sister Tori. This level is located after the P.E.A.R.L. boss fight.

But that's not all! The new "Feline" skin is introduced. Hopefully you can figure out how to unlock it.

Have fun!

notes.title: New Level: CliffHanger
notes.content:
Hello!

Yes! As promised, PsiloSybil development continues. The game now ships with a [b]new exciting level called CliffHanger[/b]. I'm going to showcase it myself soon enough whenever I get some more free time, but it was more important to me to have it ready and playable.

You can find the new level right before Stone Cold. Note that until you've beaten it, you cannot access later levels; however, your previous progress on those levels will [i]not[/i] be erased. Your savefiles will always be safe.

Have fun with it. It's a toughie for sure. 

If you spot glitches, please don't freak out -- mistakes happen, just let me know and I'll fix them right away.
